Reference

Tracing & metrics

PCS emits structured tracing events, gated behind one feature flag. pcs-core emits; pcs-service exports.

In one line
A nested span tree, a fmt subscriber, optional OTLP span export, and a Prometheus endpoint carrying nineteen series
You need
The tracing feature on pcs-core or pcs-service; the service feature turns it on for you
Read this if
You are wiring a subscriber, picking a RUST_LOG filter, pointing spans at a collector, or scraping /metrics

Where instrumentation comes from

Two things leave a running PCS process. tracing events and spans go to whatever subscriber you installed, and on to an OTLP collector when one is configured. Prometheus metrics go to the /metrics route on the service's HTTP control plane. One value crosses between them: pcs_stage_duration_seconds is measured from the lifetime of the pipeline.stage span.

the work being observed emission and export the processor, logging across the seam

The tracing feature

Both crates declare it, and it is off by default in pcs-core (default = ["runtime"]). In pcs-service the service feature includes tracing, and the pcs-service binary requires service, so the shipped binary always has instrumentation compiled in.

TOMLas declared; the service list is abridged
# crates/pcs-core/Cargo.toml
tracing = ["dep:tracing"]

# crates/pcs-service/Cargo.toml
tracing = ["dep:tracing", "pcs-core/tracing"]
service = ["pcs-core/io", "distributed", "parquet-checkpoint", "tracing", "dep:pcs-config", ...]
Constraint

This is a compile-time switch, not a runtime one. Every emission site sits inside #[cfg(feature = "tracing")], so with the feature off the call and its field formatting are absent from the binary. There is no disabled-level cost to pay, and emission cannot be turned back on without rebuilding.

Two sites keep a fallback for the feature-off build, because losing them silently would be worse than the dependency. HostIo::log falls back to eprintln! so processor log lines are never dropped, and DistributedRunner's claim-release path prints to stderr so a failed release is always visible.

Inside a .wasm processor the feature is never available: pcs-processor pins its dependency as pcs-core = { default-features = false, features = ["processor"] }. A processor reports through the host-io imports instead: log and metric, which the host bridges into its own subscriber.

A processor's println! goes nowhere. The host builds each processor's WASI context with WasiCtxBuilder::new().build() and never calls inherit_stderr(). That builder's documented default discards everything written to stdout and stderr, so println! and eprintln! inside a processor vanish. host-io::log is the only channel out.

The spans and events, module by module

Nine span names, plus flat events across fourteen targets. pipeline.run, pipeline.stage and system.execute come from pcs-core's execution path at info, and task_attempt comes from the retry driver inside them, also at info but only on a retry. The host adds five, all at debug: workflow.batch around one iteration, source.drain, runtime.run, sink.write, and processor.batch around one out-of-process processor call. One whole tree of those five opens per item, so the default log_level="info" materialises none of them and log_level="debug" is what brings the per-item waterfall back. Every host span carries workflow, the declared workflow id, and each node's span carries that node's declared id. Field names below are the exact keys the macros record, so they are what you match on in a JSON log pipeline.

TargetLevelsWhat it reports, and with which fields
pcs_core::pipeline::execution info spans Three nested spans per run: pipeline.run with pipeline, stages and rows; pipeline.stage with stage (0-based) and systems; and system.execute with system, the name from SystemMeta. The parallel-stage fan-out re-enters the stage span inside each spawn_blocking closure, so a sliced system's attempts stay under the right parent.
pcs_core::retry info span on retries, warn, error The task_attempt span at info, carrying attempt (1-based) and max_attempts. It opens only on a retry: a first attempt that succeeds opens no span, so a clean run produces none. Then a warn per failed-but-retryable attempt with error, attempt, max_attempts, delay_ms, and an error on exhaustion with error and attempts. Both the async and the blocking driver emit it, from one shared attempt counter.
pcs_core::windows::system warn Rows dropped because their timestamp was null: component, time_field, null_count. Needs the windows feature too.
pcs_service::service::standalone debug spans, info, warn, error One workflow.batch span per iteration with workflow, iteration and rows, one source.drain per source with workflow, source, component and rows, one runtime.run per processor with workflow, processor, rows_in and rows_out, and one sink.write per sink with workflow, sink, component and rows, in topological order. Every iteration event names the batch span as its parent, so the whole iteration is one trace. The busiest module, 15 event sites.
pcs_service::service::stream debug spans, info, warn, error The same span set per arriving item, minus source.drain: the wait for input precedes the item and would otherwise dominate its latency. Because those spans are debug and the default level omits them, every error and warning here names its own workflow, iteration and node rather than relying on a parent span's fields, and renders as a root record in the Logs tab. Events carry source_name, sink_name, component, error.
pcs_service::distributed::runner debug spans, info, warn, error One workflow.batch span per claimed batch with workflow, claim and rows, holding one runtime.run. Expired-lease sweeps and every release-instead-of-ack path: reclaimed_count, claim_id, error.
pcs_service::distributed::consensus::transport::server info, debug, warn The Raft TCP accept loop: addr on bind, peer per connection, error on frame, decode and encode failures.
pcs_service::distributed::parquet_checkpoint debug A parent-directory fsync that failed after a checkpoint write: error. Needs the parquet-checkpoint feature.
pcs_service::wasm::host_impl trace–error The processor's own host-io::log lines, re-emitted at the level the processor asked for and tagged pipeline and target. They land inside that batch's processor.batch span, because the runtime re-enters it on the blocking thread the guest call runs on. A host-io::metric call records the pcs_processor_metric histogram, labelled with the metric name, and also emits a trace event with metric and value.
pcs_service::wasm::runner debug span, warn One processor.batch span per run-batch call, covering the IPC encode, the guest call and the IPC decode: workflow, processor, rows_in, rows_out, systems_run, retries, guest_wall_us, the last four read back off the WIT run-metrics record. The warn covers building the template dataset: describe() failed, or one component's schema would not parse (component, error).
pcs_service::plugin::runtime debug span, debug The same processor.batch span for a native plugin, with plugin_wall_us in place of guest_wall_us. The debug reports a loaded plugin's plugin, version, stateful and components.
pcs_service::service::http, ::shutdown info, debug, warn, error Control-plane bind and clean shutdown, signal receipt, and the 30-second shutdown budget being exceeded.
pcs_service::commands::serve info, error Binary startup (node_id), which of signal-or-runner-exit fired first, and the exit path.
tower_http::trace info, debug Not PCS code, but it is in the output: build_router installs TraceLayer::new_for_http(), so each request to /health, /ready, /metrics or /status gets a span and request/response events.

Spans nest, so a JSON log line carries its whole ancestry and a collector can reconstruct one trace per iteration. The host draws the outer three levels.

A native pipeline's pipeline.run nests three levels further. A processor opens the same three inside the guest, where the host cannot see them, so a WASM processor is one span rather than a subtree.

Installing a subscriber

PCS never installs a subscriber for you when you use it as a library. Without one, every event is discarded and you see nothing. The minimum is tracing-subscriber with the fmt and env-filter features.

TOMLpath dependencies — these crates are not published
[dependencies]
pcs-core = { path = "../pcs-core", features = ["tracing"] }
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["fmt", "env-filter"] }
Rustinstall once, before the first pipeline runs
use tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    tracing_subscriber::fmt()
        .with_env_filter(EnvFilter::from_default_env())
        .init();

    // build and run your pipeline; the pipeline.run span tree and any
    // window or runner events now reach stdout
}

The service binary does this for you. pcs-service serve calls init_logging as step 3, before anything else can emit, and treats a second call as an error because the global subscriber is already installed. It stacks four layers: the EnvFilter, the fmt layer, SpanMetricsLayer for the stage histogram, and an OTLP layer when otlp_endpoint is set.

Rustwhat the binary calls
use pcs_service::service::config::ObservabilityConfig;
use pcs_service::service::logging::init_logging;

let cfg = ObservabilityConfig::default();  // Pretty, "info", no span export
let telemetry = init_logging(&cfg, node_id)?;

// ... run the service ...

// Flush exported spans. Dropping the guard is not enough, because
// set_tracer_provider keeps a clone in a process-lifetime static.
telemetry.shutdown().await;

Level, format and span export from the config file

The observability node has four keys: two for the log stream and two for span export. There is no per-module table, because module filtering is the filter string's job.

KDLspan export is off unless otlp_endpoint is set
observability {
    log_format "pretty"   // use "json" in production log aggregators
    log_level "info"
    otlp_endpoint "http://collector:4318"
    trace_sample_ratio 0.1
}
KeyValuesDefault
log_format "pretty" or "json". Pretty enables ANSI colour only when stdout is a terminal; JSON emits one object per record. "pretty"
log_level Any EnvFilter directive string, so "debug" and "warn,pcs_service::service::standalone=debug" are both valid here. "info"
otlp_endpoint Collector base URL for OTLP over HTTP. The exporter appends /v1/traces, so give it the collector root. Omit the key and no span exporter is built. none
trace_sample_ratio Parent-based trace-id-ratio sampling, 0.0 to 1.0. A value outside that range fails startup with a configuration error. 1.0

init_logging turns log_level into the filter pcs=<log_level>,tower_http=info,warn. Directives match the event target by prefix, so the single pcs directive covers both pcs_core::… and pcs_service::…, and everything else in the dependency tree stays at warn.

RUST_LOG wins outright: the environment filter is tried first, and the directive above is only the fallback when RUST_LOG is unset. Both keys can also be overridden per-invocation, by flag or by environment variable.

Bashthree orders of precedence, and real module paths
# CLI flag beats the config file
pcs-service serve --config standalone.kdl --log-format json --log-level debug

# ... and so do PCS_LOG_FORMAT / PCS_LOG_LEVEL
PCS_LOG_LEVEL=debug pcs-service serve --config standalone.kdl

# Span export can be turned on without touching the config file
pcs-service serve --config standalone.kdl --otlp-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:4318

# RUST_LOG beats all of them: only the standalone runner, everything else quiet
RUST_LOG="warn,pcs_service::service::standalone=info" \
  pcs-service serve --config standalone.kdl

# The Raft accept loop, including per-connection debug events
RUST_LOG="warn,pcs_service::distributed::consensus::transport=debug" \
  pcs-service serve --config cluster.kdl

# Processor log lines and processor metric calls, nothing else
RUST_LOG="off,pcs_service::wasm::host_impl=trace" \
  pcs-service serve --config standalone_wasm.kdl

The Prometheus endpoint

The service binary builds a prometheus::Registry, hands it to opentelemetry_prometheus::exporter(), wraps that in an SdkMeterProvider, installs it as the global OpenTelemetry meter provider, and then calls pcs_service::metrics::init() to build every instrument. The /metrics handler gathers that same registry and encodes it with prometheus::TextEncoder, returning text/plain; version=0.0.4.

The exporter is built with without_counter_suffixes(), because the instrument names already end in _total.

Bashdefault bind is 0.0.0.0:8080
curl -s localhost:8080/metrics | grep '^pcs_'
# pcs_liveness_counter{otel_scope_name="pcs"} 6
# pcs_workflow_runs_total{otel_scope_name="pcs"} 50
# pcs_ready{otel_scope_name="pcs"} 1
# pcs_uptime_seconds{otel_scope_name="pcs"} 5.0141387

curl -s localhost:8080/status | jq .standalone
# {
#   "iterations": 7,
#   "rows_processed": 7000,
#   "source_batches_drained": 7,
#   "sink_batches_written": 7,
#   "iteration_errors": 0
# }

/metrics shares the router with /health, /ready and /status, all four behind a 10-second timeout layer. Nineteen series are declared and every one has a writer. A series reaches the scrape output once its writer has recorded a value, so the pcs_raft_* gauges appear on a cluster node and the pcs_processor_* series appear once a .wasm processor has run a batch.

Eleven of those series are also recorded a second time under the id that wrote them: pcs_rows_processed_total and pcs_source_batches_drained_total under source, pcs_sink_batches_written_total under sink, the six pcs_processor_* series under processor, and the two workflow counters under workflow. The attribute value is the id the config declared for that node (or workflow).

Attribution is additive, not a replacement. The unattributed write always happens, and it is the process-wide total across every node of that kind, which is what a scrape has always read. An existing query keeps working untouched, at the cost that summing the attributed and unattributed forms double counts. A node id is a dimension on nine existing instruments. A workflow id is a dimension on the two workflow counters. The one attributed-only series, pcs_window_watermark_seconds, is the exception: a watermark belongs to one node's merged inbound stream, so there is no unattributed form to double count.

SeriesTypeWritten by
pcs_workflow_runs_totalcounterThe standalone, stream and cluster runners, once per completed run. Also recorded under workflow, the id the config declared for that workflow.
pcs_workflow_errors_totalcounterThe same three runners, when a processor run itself fails. Source and sink drain failures stay on /status, so this series is alertable on its own. Also recorded under workflow, the id the config declared for that workflow.
pcs_stage_duration_secondshistogramSpanMetricsLayer, from the lifetime of each pipeline.stage span. Unattributed: the layer discards that span's fields, so there is nothing to attribute from.
pcs_source_batches_drained_totalcounterThe three runners, per non-empty source drain or claimed partition. Also recorded under source.
pcs_sink_batches_written_totalcounterThe standalone and stream runners, also recorded under sink. Cluster mode has no sinks, so it stays at zero there.
pcs_rows_processed_totalcounterThe three runners, rows a source drained into the workflow. Also recorded under source.
pcs_liveness_countergaugeThe watchdog task, once a second.
pcs_readygaugeThe watchdog task: 1 once the runner is spawned.
pcs_uptime_secondsgaugeThe watchdog task.
pcs_raft_commit_indexgaugeThe cluster runner's Raft recorder, once a second from the driver handle.
pcs_raft_termgaugeThe same recorder.
pcs_raft_leader_idgaugeThe same recorder. It reports -1 when there is no leader, so a lost election shows up instead of a stale id.
pcs_processor_batch_duration_secondshistogramThe wasm and native plugin hosts, from the batch's run metrics. Also recorded under processor, which is the dashboard's per-node latency.
pcs_processor_rows_in_totalcounterThe wasm and native plugin hosts, from the batch's run metrics. Also recorded under processor.
pcs_processor_rows_out_totalcounterThe wasm and native plugin hosts, from the batch's run metrics. Also recorded under processor, which is what rates that processor's outbound edge on the dashboard.
pcs_processor_systems_run_totalcounterThe wasm and native plugin hosts, from the batch's run metrics. Also recorded under processor.
pcs_processor_retries_totalcounterThe wasm and native plugin hosts, from the batch's run metrics. Also recorded under processor.
pcs_processor_metrichistogramEvery host-io::metric call, labelled metric with the processor's own name. Distinct names are capped at 256. The second record carries metric and processor, sorted by key.
pcs_window_watermark_secondsgaugeThe standalone and stream runners, once per processor call, for every processor node whose config declares a window block. Recorded only under processor: the maximum time_field event timestamp observed across the node's merged inbound rows, in epoch seconds.

/health is the one to alert on: it is backed by the watchdog counter, so it goes stale if the main loop wedges. /ready and /status both mean less than they look; see what is still missing.

The in-process inspector reads these same nineteen series and introduces none of its own, so a dashboard number and a /metrics number are always the same value. See Observability.

What is still missing

Five things an operator may expect and will not find, and one that appears twice.

  • Export covers spans only. otlp_endpoint installs a span exporter. Metrics stay pull-only on /metrics: there is no OTLP metrics exporter and no push path.
  • /status answers "cluster": null in cluster mode. ServiceState.cluster_probe is never populated, so the rich Raft snapshot the type describes is unreachable over HTTP. The three pcs_raft_* gauges carry term, commit index and leader instead, read straight from the driver handle.
  • /ready reports the process, not the workflow. The flag flips as soon as the runner task is spawned, so it never means an iteration succeeded.
  • A native plugin's own metric names are log lines. The C ABI's metric callback is the counterpart of host-io::metric, but it emits a trace event and writes no series: the six pcs_processor_* names are host-reserved for the per-batch numbers the runtime reports, which a native plugin records exactly like a WASM processor.
  • pcs_stage_duration_seconds follows the tracing filter. It is derived from the pipeline.stage span, and the EnvFilter is subscriber-wide. A filter that suppresses pcs_core at span level stops the histogram too.
  • An attributed series overlaps its own total. The form with no attributes is already the sum across every node of that kind, and the attributed form is one node's share, so a query that sums both counts every value twice. Select the empty attribute value, source="", processor="", sink="" or workflow="", for the process-wide number.
